Situation1: Help each other in times of need or emotional distress.
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: A friend on their way to the airport calls, thinking they left their passport at home, and asks if you can check and bring it to them right away.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was about to leave the house. It was my friend, panicked, saying she was already halfway to the airport and thought she’d left her passport on my kitchen table after our coffee this morning. She begged me to check and, if it was there, to bring it to her as fast as possible—her flight was in two hours. I promised I’d look, but as I hung up, I heard my sister crying in her room. She’d just gotten some bad news about her job and needed me. I could hear her muffled sobs through the door, and I knew she expected me to sit with her, to listen and comfort her like I always did. My heart twisted. My friend was counting on me to save her trip, but my sister needed me right now, too. I stood in the hallway, torn, feeling the weight of both their needs pressing down on me, unsure which way to turn.
